info.title: NessGate API
info.description: The open, neutral compatibility resolver for the agentic web. Given a domain, NessGate reads whatever that domain already publishes across the standard machine-discovery locations (llms.txt, ARD / ai-catalog.json, A2A agent card, RFC 9727 API catalog, ai-info.json, OpenAPI, Open Resource Discovery, AWP manifest, RFC 6415 host-meta) and returns one normalized answer, each record carrying a sourceUrl back to the domain. NessGate stores nothing, never crawls or indexes, and makes no ownership or safety claim. Read endpoints are public, unauthenticated, and CORS-open. The response contract is stable and additive: new optional fields may appear; clients must ignore unknown fields.

get.summary: Resolve a domain to the machine-readable resources it publishes
get.description: Reads what the domain itself publishes at the standard machine-discovery locations (llms.txt, ARD/ai-catalog, A2A agent card, RFC 9727 api-catalog, ai-info.json, openapi.json (and .yaml/.yml, detected via the document's own top-level marker), Open Resource Discovery, AWP manifest awp.json, RFC 6415 host-meta) and returns one normalized answer. Provenance is always "self-published": each record carries a sourceUrl back to the domain so the caller can verify. "Found" means the location exists and its content parses (JSON, or non-HTML text); it does not assert protocol conformance. Nothing is stored or indexed; results are computed live and cached for 10 minutes. When the exact host publishes nothing and its homepage redirects within the same registrable domain (apex to www./subdomain), the canonical host is probed for llms.txt and ard.json as a bounded fallback; cross-registrable-domain redirects are never followed here.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Domain name, e.g. example.com. Scheme, path, port, and a leading www. are ignored; ASCII/punycode form required.

parameters.name: fast
parameters.description: Set to 1 for fast mode: SKIPS the alternate ARD locators (homepage rel="ard" link and robots Agentmap) to save 2 requests. This is a labeled performance trade and is NOT fully ARD v0.91-conformant (a catalog advertised only via rel="ard" can be missed) — the response is flagged mode:"fast" and 'checked' omits ard-link/ard-agentmap. Default (omit ?fast) is complete and conformant.

parameters.name: mcp
parameters.description: Set to 1 to introspect DECLARED MCP endpoints read-only via the protocol's own handshake (initialize + tools/list only — never tools/call, no credentials, POSTs never follow redirects). HTTPS endpoints on the queried registrable domain only, max 3 per resolution, 256 KB response cap. Declared tools land verbatim in the resource's capabilities; the response is labeled introspected:["mcp"]. Default (omit ?mcp) never introspects.

parameters.name: verify
parameters.description: Set to 1 for a labeled reachability pass: surfaces this resolution already fetched are marked reachability ok with NO extra request (the fetch is the evidence); MCP records reuse introspection results when present; declared pointers get ONE safe probe each (HEAD, then a bounded GET when HEAD is unsupported — never a POST, never an execution), capped at 8, mapped to ok | auth-required | not-found | unreachable with a per-record checkedAt. Absent reachability = not checked. ok means the endpoint answered a safe request — never that operations succeed or the caller is authorized. Cross-registrable targets are probed only because the publisher itself declared them. Default (omit ?verify) never probes.

200.description: Observation complete. An empty discovered array is still a successful answer.

outcome.description: The single honest outcome label. found = validated resources exist. none-found = the checks completed and confirmed no supported declaration at the locations checked (clean 404s count as answers). blocked = nothing found AND refusals (auth/rate/5xx, timeouts, network failures) were at least as common as clean answers - the checks were prevented, so absence is UNKNOWN.

blockedProbes.description: Present when any probe was refused: the count of refused probes, disclosed even when the outcome is none-found so uncertainty is never hidden.

mode.description: Present only when ?fast=1 was used: signals the alternate ARD locators were skipped (not fully ARD-conformant). Absent for the default complete mode.

introspected.description: Present only when ?mcp=1 was used: read-only MCP introspection ran on declared endpoints. Absent by default.

verified.description: Present only when ?verify=1 was used: the labeled reachability pass ran. Absent by default.

discovered.description: The routing map: which standards the domain publishes, and where.

resources.description: The normalized union of what those documents contain, flattened into one list.

checked.description: Every standard NessGate probed for, so an empty result is still informative.

400.description: Input is not a valid domain.

get.summary: Evidence-based delegated resolution across declared pointers and registries
get.description: Everything /discover returns, plus bounded DELEGATED discovery: follows the explicit machine-readable pointers a domain declares (llms.txt index links, ARD/api-catalog entries) to arbitrary chain depth within the request/byte/host/time budgets (loop-detected, per-hop validated, runaway backstop) — cross-host only where the publisher named the target — and federates the official MCP Registry for the domain's verified reverse-DNS namespace. Every resource carries an 'evidence' class (publisher-hosted | publisher-declared | namespace-verified) and a 'provenance' chain. Strictly bounded (depth <=2, <=8 hosts, <=24 requests, global byte cap, SSRF checks per hop); stateless, no crawling, no AI, no ownership claim. With ?org=1 (Organization Discovery), additionally probes a bounded set of plausible same-registrable-domain hosts (homepage-linked subdomains plus a small conventional shortlist) and reports only verified resources as evidence same-domain-host. Rate limited 60/hour/IP; cached 10 minutes.

parameters.name: org
parameters.description: Set to 1 to enable Organization Discovery: probe a bounded set of plausible same-registrable-domain hosts (homepage-linked subdomains with developer/doc-facing labels first, then a conventional shortlist incl. docs./developers./cloud., max 6 hosts x 3 paths) and report only verified resources, labelled evidence same-domain-host. Hosts probed are listed in orgChecked; hosts that refused or blackholed every probe are listed in orgBlocked (absence there is unknown; a clean 404 counts as answered). A homepage redirect to a different registrable domain is reported as homepageRedirect {from,to} - an observation of the publisher's own configuration, never merged into resources.

parameters.name: related
parameters.description: Set to 1 for Related Discovery: a separate cross-registrable-domain layer returned in related[] (never mixed with resources[]). Classes: publisher-declared-related (the queried domain serves a purpose-built declaration such as a legacy Related Website Set file; hyperlinks never qualify), registry-verified-related (a domain-verifying registry names the specific host, attributed), infrastructure-correlated-candidate (caller candidates with a cited technical signal). Technical signals are corroborating only and never mean official or same organization. Bounded, max 5 related hosts.

200.description: Evidence-based observation. An empty resources array is still a successful answer.

outcome.description: The single honest outcome label; /explore adds incomplete = budgets or the deadline cut the walk before it finished, so an empty result may just be unfinished.

blockedProbes.description: Present when any probe was refused: count of refused probes (uncertainty is never hidden).

related.description: Only with ?related=1: cross-registrable-domain entries, each { host, class: publisher-declared-related | registry-verified-related | infrastructure-correlated-candidate, declaration?, attribution?, signals[], resources[] }. Separate from resources[]; signals are corroborating only.

resources.description: Normalized records, each with an evidence class, a provenance chain, and depth.

evidence.description: candidate = a caller-suggested URL (via POST {"candidates":[...]}) that NessGate fetched and confirmed is machine-readable; relationship to the domain is unverified.

provenance.description: The chain of URLs/registry hops by which this record was reached.

attribution.description: For namespace-verified records: who verified the namespace (attributed to the registry, not NessGate).

400.description: Input is not a valid domain.

post.description: JSON-RPC 2.0 over the MCP Streamable HTTP transport. Stateless, no authentication. Exposes one read-only tool, discover_domain, which returns the same normalized answer as GET /discover/{domain}.

schema.description: A single JSON-RPC 2.0 message (initialize, tools/list, tools/call, ping).

405.description: GET is not supported; use POST.

Resource.description: A normalized record. NessGate reuses each source's own labels and adds source/sourceUrl.

source.description: Which standard this record came from.

sourceUrl.description: The native document the record was read from — authoritative; follow it to verify.

type.description: An open label taken from the source. Not a closed set.

class.description: How much NessGate verified this resource (no extra requests): verified-publisher-location = the surface NessGate fetched and validated on the domain's own registrable domain; publisher-declared = declared inside a fetched catalog, target on the same registrable domain, target not itself fetched; declared-external-pointer = declared but the target is on a different registrable domain (unverified); unsupported = no usable target URL. A 'third-party association' is an /explore concept; /discover never fetches declared pointers, so it emits no 'inaccessible' class.

capabilities.description: Verbatim publisher-declared capabilities from the source document itself — OpenAPI operations (method, path, operationId, summary) or A2A/GB-Z agent-card skills (id, name, description, tags). Copied 1:1 from the publisher's own words; never inferred, renamed, or reclassified. Absent when the source declares none. Capped at 40 (capabilitiesTruncated flags the cap).

capabilitiesTruncated.description: True when the publisher declared more capabilities than the cap; the list is a labeled prefix, never a silent truncation.

introspection.description: Only with ?mcp=1, on declared MCP endpoint resources: the result of the read-only MCP handshake (initialize + tools/list only — no tool execution, no credentials). ok:true carries the negotiated protocolVersion and the server's own serverInfo; ok:false carries status: auth-required | legacy-transport | error. Declared tools land verbatim in capabilities.

security.description: Verbatim declared security schemes (OpenAPI components.securitySchemes / Swagger-2 securityDefinitions): { name, type, scheme, in }. Capped at 40; securityTruncated flags the cap.

securityTruncated.description: True when the spec declares more security schemes than the cap; the list is a labeled prefix, never a silent truncation.

reachability.description: Only with ?verify=1. ok = answered a safe request (never asserts operations succeed or authorization); auth-required = 401/407 or a WWW-Authenticate header (protocol evidence, never assumed); rate-limited = 429 (alive; Retry-After captured as evidence, never acted on); blocked = anti-bot protection RELIABLY identified via a conservative signal list (challenge headers/markers) — NessGate identifies walls, never bypasses them; not-found = 404/410 (declared, nothing there); unreachable = network failures/timeouts/5xx; unknown = a denial whose cause cannot be established (e.g. a bare 403 — auth and bot-walls both use it, and NessGate never assumes either). Absent = not checked.

checkedAt.description: Only with ?verify=1: when this record's reachability was determined (ISO timestamp).

evidence.description: Only with ?verify=1: why the reachability label was chosen — { status?, signal?, retryAfterSeconds? }. signal is a NAME only (e.g. cf-challenge, www-authenticate, fetched-this-resolution, mcp-introspection); response content is never stored or returned.
